summary: Audit completed with 5 findings originating from root devDependencies at baseline commit 1df8543. No new runtime dependencies from WEB-01A introduce any vulnerabilities. npm audit fix was not run per repository policy.

findings.title: When Vitest UI server is listening, arbitrary file can be read and executed
findings.riskAssessment: Low operational risk in development. Project test scripts strictly execute CLI mode (`vitest run`), never running the vulnerable Vitest UI web server (`vitest --ui`).

findings.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
findings.riskAssessment: Low. Redirect mock features of @vitest/mocker are not utilized in repository test suites.

findings.title: vite: `server.fs.deny` bypass on Windows alternate paths
findings.riskAssessment: Mitigated. Vite dev server binds exclusively to 127.0.0.1 and is protected by localProxy Host/Origin guard.

findings.title: launch-editor: NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC path handling on Windows
findings.riskAssessment: Low. The launch-editor functionality is not used or invoked in test/build pipelines.

findings.title: Vite Vulnerable to Path Traversal in Optimized Deps `.map` Handling
findings.riskAssessment: Low. Local development optimization only; production builds produce static bundle assets without map leakage.

findings.title: esbuild enables any website to send any requests to the development server and read the response
findings.riskAssessment: Mitigated. esbuild server is not exposed directly; Vite runs with custom local proxy rejecting foreign origins.
